question: Should instruction-aware query formatting become a public `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate` and Plugin SDK contract, or remain provider-owned without a new generic configuration/API surface?
rationale: The model-specific behavior is useful and source-supported, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config and Plugin SDK surfaces; code review cannot choose that permanent product boundary safely.

options.title: Accept The Opt-In Contract
options.body: Keep the default-disabled setting and shared helper, document the supported model families precisely, and require current-head upgrade and live behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Formatting Provider-Owned
options.body: Remove the generic config and SDK additions, then implement any approved template behavior inside the owning providers through an existing or narrower provider-specific seam.

options.title: Pause The Direction
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it without merging until maintainers want to support model-id-based query formatting as a maintained OpenClaw capability.

recommendation.title: Accept The Opt-In Contract
recommendation.body: Keep the default-disabled setting and shared helper, document the supported model families precisely, and require current-head upgrade and live behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The provider-plugin embedding refactor and public boundary history make this the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
